record.paper_title: Open problems on Steiner trees and maximal distance minimizers
record.original_question: For finite M⊂R^2 of cardinality n, how does the explicit algebraic description of an MDM Sigma depend on M through the degrees of the resulting equations? For rational coordinates, what is the largest degree of the extension of Q generated by G_Sigma?

evidence.quote: Question 1.7. Let M⊂R^2 be a finite set of cardinality n. How does the explicit description of a minimizer Σ depend on M in terms of the degrees of the resulting equations?

artifact.self_contained_problem:
Setting. For a nonempty compact set M ⊂ ℝ² and r > 0, a maximal distance minimizer for M with radius r is a connected compact set Σ ⊂ ℝ² of minimal one-dimensional Hausdorff length such that

  max_{x∈M} dist(x, Σ) ≤ r,

where dist(x, Σ) = inf_{y∈Σ} |x − y|. It is known that such a minimizer Σ exists, is a finite topological graph, and that its edges consist of straight line segments and arcs of circles of radius r; we denote by G_Σ the finite set of all points of Σ which are vertices (endpoints or branching points) of this graph together with the centers of the circular arcs and the tangency points of the arcs with the segments. The geometry of Σ is encoded by a finite system of polynomial equations in the coordinates of the points of G_Σ, derived from the local first-order optimality conditions (angle conditions at branching points, tangency between segments and arcs, and the constraint that the r-neighborhood of Σ covers M).

Problem.
(a) Let M ⊂ ℝ² be a finite set of cardinality n. Describe explicitly, as a function of n, the degrees of the polynomial equations that determine a maximal distance minimizer Σ for M; in particular, give a sharp (or as sharp as possible) upper bound, depending only on n, for the degrees of the equations needed to specify Σ.

(b) Assume in addition that every point of M has rational coordinates. Considering all such configurations M of cardinality n and all maximal distance minimizers Σ for M, determine the largest possible degree, as a function of n, of the algebraic extension of ℚ generated over ℚ by the coordinates of all points of G_Σ.
artifact.status_search_result: The problem is posed as an open question in a recent collection of open problems on Steiner trees and maximal distance minimizers (Teplitskaya, 2025). Related work (e.g. the overview of maximal distance minimizers and inverse problems) discusses that minimizers reduce to algebraic systems generalizing Alhazen-type quartic equations, but no general degree bound or extension-degree formula in terms of n has been established.
